messages:
jin: Ran a profiling sweep on the TP all-reduce path this morning. Noticed a tail latency increase for small-message workloads (~<1KB). Attaching quick logs and notes.

perf-bot: Regression alert: +12% p95 on tp_allreduce_small_msg after commit f3a2b1 (2026-03-17 09:12 UTC).

alex: Can you paste the logs? :eyes:

jin: ```profile snippet:
tp_allreduce_run id=ae3
mode=ring
msg_sizes=[128,256,512]
p95=52ms (baseline 45ms)
KV cache hitrate=6%
batch_size=2
kernel=allreduce_ring
extra: memcpy_time=8ms, kernel_time=22ms, comm_wait=15ms
```

maya: Huh. Ring is usually more efficient for large contiguous buffers, but for many small msgs tree reduces hop latency. Did the kernel-selection thresholds change in that commit?

sam: I inspected f3a2b1 — we lowered the ring preference threshold from 1024->512 and also tweaked the batching heuristic (max_batch_tokens 2048->1024). That will push more small-message ops onto ring and increase #allreduces.

jin: Exactly. KV cache hitrate dropped a bit too which reduced prefix coalescing. More separate allreduces = worse tail.

alex: Quick experiment idea: revert the ring threshold to 1024 and restore max_batch_tokens to 2048 on a canary. Also compare NCCL algorithm knobs (NCCL_ALGO=tree) as a fallback.

jin: Did a 10min canary locally: setting selector.threshold=1024 moved ~70% of small ops to tree and p95 dropped to 46ms. Large sequence throughput stayed within 1%.

maya: Good. We should also add better telemetry: log chosen_kernel,msg_size,batch_id,kv_hit boolean into the trace so we can correlate p95 by series.

sam: I'll add a microtrace in kernel_selector and gate it behind exp flag. Also we should surface per-allreduce duration in the console (per-request breakdown).

alex: One more: check NCCL chunking/async progress flags. For tiny messages, the cost is dominated by latency not bandwidth — kernel-level scheduling (launch latency) matters. Maybe change kernel to a tree implementation that has fewer sequential hops.

jin: I captured an nvprof NVTX timeline. Overlap between compute and comm is near zero for these runs, which means batching changes killed overlap.

maya: On overlap: maybe the runtime's kernel selection now prefers fused kernels that are less preemptible; that reduces overlap. We should add a metric: comm_time / (comm_time+compute_time) per step.

sam: Action items I pulled: 1) revert threshold->1024 on canary (sam) 2) add kernel_selector microtrace (sam) 3) add perf-harness regression test for small-msg p95 <= baseline+5% (alex) 4) NVTX profiler run with kvcache ranges (maya) 5) evaluate NCCL_ALGO env fallback (jin).

perf-bot: Canary rolled to 20% for revert-threshold experiment. Watching metrics: p95, throughput, kv_hitrate. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jin: Thanks. If we see stable improvement on canary, we can promote and then follow up with better heuristics (e.g., dynamic threshold based on observed msg_size histogram and kv_hit rate).

maya: I'll paste nvprof excerpts in this thread once done. Early note: when kv_hit >= 30% the effective msgsize coalesces and ring becomes preferable. So dynamic decision sounds right. :+1:

alex: Nice. Also add a short note in the runtime changelog so on-call knows about kernel-selection flip cause.

jin: Agreed. Will file a tiny postmortem if this goes to prod.

maya: nvprof snippets incoming in ~30m.

sam: starting the selector microtrace PR now.

jin: great, thx everyone.
